question: How does Next.js work?
reference_points: React framework that handles rendering, routing and optimization automatically
Pre-renders pages via SSR or SSG for speed and SEO
File-based routing maps files to URLs
Automatic code splitting loads only needed JavaScript
Built-in bundling, minification and image optimization

question: What is Next.js and how is it different from React?
reference_points: React is a UI library; Next.js is a framework built on React
Adds routing, server rendering, static generation and data fetching
Provides built-in metadata, image optimization and code splitting
Plain React (e.g. Vite) requires choosing your own router, rendering model and deployment setup

question: What is Styled JSX in Next.js?
reference_points: CSS-in-JS library bundled with Next.js
Creates encapsulated, component-scoped styles
Styles do not leak into other components
Styles can be added or removed without affecting unrelated parts

question: What is the purpose of the app and pages directories in Next.js?
reference_points: Both directories define routes through the file system
pages/ is the older Pages Router
app/ is the newer App Router using React Server Components
Files inside map to URL segments
Both can coexist in one project during migration

question: What is the App Router in Next.js?
reference_points: Modern router based on the app/ directory
Built on React Server Components
Supports nested layouts, loading UI and error boundaries
Supports route handlers and streaming

question: What is file-based routing in Next.js?
reference_points: Folder and file structure defines URL structure
In App Router a segment is public only if it has page.tsx or page.js
In Pages Router every file in pages/ becomes a route
Removes the need for manual route configuration

question: How do you create dynamic routes in Next.js?
reference_points: Use square brackets in folder or file name, e.g. [slug]
Value is passed to the page through params
Catch-all segments use [...slug]
Optional catch-all uses [[...slug]]
Used when URL values are unknown ahead of time

question: What is the difference between SSR, SSG, CSR and ISR?
reference_points: SSR renders HTML on the server for each request
SSG generates HTML at build time
CSR sends a JavaScript shell and renders mainly in the browser
ISR serves static output and regenerates it after revalidation
Next.js can mix these patterns per route

question: What is the loading.tsx file in Next.js?
reference_points: Defines loading UI for a route segment
Shown while the route or nested content loads
Built on React Suspense
Enables streaming so users see partial content early

question: What is not-found.tsx in Next.js?
reference_points: Defines the 404 UI for a route segment
Triggered by calling notFound() from next/navigation
Used when the route exists but the resource does not
Global 404 handled by app/not-found.tsx

question: What is the Link component in Next.js?
reference_points: next/link enables client-side navigation without full reload
Prefetches routes likely to be visited
Used for internal navigation, normal <a> for external links

question: What is the useRouter hook and how do you navigate programmatically in Next.js?
reference_points: Used in Client Components for programmatic navigation
Methods include push, replace, back and refresh
App Router imports it from next/navigation
Server code uses redirect() instead

question: What is the difference between push and replace in useRouter?
reference_points: push adds a new entry to the browser history stack
replace overwrites the current history entry
After replace the back button skips the replaced page
Use replace for flows like login redirects

question: How do you add metadata for SEO in Next.js?
reference_points: Export a static metadata object from a page or layout
Use async generateMetadata() when data depends on params or fetching
Replaces next/head in the App Router
Covers title, description and Open Graph tags

question: What is the Head component and next/head in Next.js?
reference_points: next/head lets Pages Router pages modify the document head
Used for title, meta and link tags
Not used in the App Router, which uses the Metadata API

question: What is the Image component in Next.js?
reference_points: next/image optimizes images automatically
Handles sizing, lazy loading and modern formats
Prevents layout shift when width and height are provided
Reduces load size of one of the heaviest page assets

question: How do you optimize and enable custom fonts in Next.js?
reference_points: next/font loads and optimizes fonts
Self-hosts fonts to avoid external requests
Reduces layout shift with generated CSS at build time
Supports Google fonts and local custom fonts

question: How do environment variables work in Next.js?
reference_points: Stored in .env files and read via process.env
Server-only variables stay on the server and suit secrets
NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix exposes variables to the browser
Never put secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables

question: How do you deploy a Next.js app?
reference_points: Run next build then host the generated output
Vercel supports all Next.js features natively
Node hosts or adapters can also run Next.js
Static export cannot support server rendering, Route Handlers or Server Actions

question: How do you enable TypeScript in a Next.js project?
reference_points: Create a tsconfig.json file or use create-next-app with TypeScript
Install typescript and @types/react and @types/node
Next.js auto-generates config and next-env.d.ts on dev start
Rename files to .ts or .tsx

question: What is the public folder in Next.js?
reference_points: Serves static files such as images, favicon and robots.txt
Files are served from the site root path
Files are not processed by the bundler

question: What is the default port of a Next.js app and how do you change it?
reference_points: Default port is 3000
Change with next dev -p <port> or --port
Or set the PORT environment variable
Can be set in package.json scripts

question: What is Fast Refresh in Next.js?
reference_points: Provides instant feedback on edits during development
Preserves component state when editing React components
Reloads fully when edits affect non-component exports
Recovers automatically from syntax and runtime errors

question: What is next.config.js used for?
reference_points: Central configuration file for Next.js
Configures redirects, rewrites, headers and env
Sets image domains, output mode and experimental features
Customizes build behavior such as Webpack

question: How do you add component-level and global CSS in Next.js?
reference_points: Component-level styles use CSS Modules (*.module.css)
CSS Modules scope class names locally
Global CSS is imported in the root layout (App Router) or _app.js (Pages Router)
Styled JSX and CSS-in-JS are alternatives

question: How do you use Tailwind CSS in Next.js?
reference_points: Install Tailwind and its PostCSS setup, or choose it in create-next-app
Configure content paths in the Tailwind config
Import Tailwind directives in a global CSS file
Use utility classes in components

question: What is the purpose of next-env.d.ts?
reference_points: Auto-generated TypeScript declaration file
References Next.js types for TypeScript
Should not be edited manually
Ensures type support for images and Next.js APIs

question: What is next/script used for?
reference_points: Optimized loading of third-party scripts
strategy prop controls timing: beforeInteractive, afterInteractive, lazyOnload
Prevents scripts from blocking page rendering
Used for analytics and widgets

question: How do you add Google Analytics to a Next.js project?
reference_points: Use the @next/third-parties Google Analytics component
Or load the gtag script with next/script
Store the measurement ID in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ environment variable
Place it in the root layout so it loads site-wide

question: What is the difference between the pages and components directories in Next.js?
reference_points: pages directory defines routes
components directory is a convention for reusable UI, not routing
Files in components do not become URLs
components folder is user-created, not special to Next.js

question: What is the Pages Router in Next.js and how do you create routes with it?
reference_points: Original Next.js router based on the pages/ directory
Each file in pages/ becomes a route
index.js maps to the folder root
Dynamic routes use [param].js

question: What are _error.js and custom 404 pages in the Pages Router?
reference_points: _error.js customizes generic error pages for server and client errors
pages/404.js creates a static custom 404 page
pages/500.js customizes server error page
Custom pages are statically generated at build time

question: What are API Routes in Next.js?
reference_points: Files inside pages/api become API endpoints
Export a handler function receiving req and res
Run only on the server and not added to client bundle
Allow backend functionality within the app

question: What are common use cases for the App Router?
reference_points: Apps needing server-rendered data with minimal client JS
Dashboards with nested layouts
Content sites using streaming and caching
Forms and mutations using Server Actions

question: How do you implement nested layouts in the App Router?
reference_points: Add layout.tsx in each route segment folder
Layouts nest automatically around child segments
Layouts persist across navigation and do not re-render
Root layout must contain html and body tags
